text: Here's how the replay works. A real variable rate is the lender's own index plus a fixed margin, and the replay needs a much longer record than that index has. So it uses a stand-in with a long U.S. record, the rate on three-month Treasury bills, and sets the margin so that Leah's rate starts at seven point five percent. From then on, her rate rises and falls exactly as much as the Treasury bill rate did. The first replay starts in January nineteen fifty-four and runs for ten years, and the next starts one month later, and so on, up to September twenty sixteen. Each one is set against the nine percent fixed loan over the same ten years. Neighbouring stretches share most of their years, so they are not independent tries, and the data is U.S. only.
